The integration of the 48V electrical system provides seamless start-stop functionality and a temporary 22 hp torque fill via the ISG.

costGuide.title: Mercedes-Benz M256 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an M256 engine typically takes 14-20 hours at £85-£110/hr (AMG/modern Mercedes specialist) - the tight packaging of the 48V components and ancillary drives makes extraction labour-intensive.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this engine is the health of the 48V Integrated Starter Generator (ISG), the electric auxiliary compressor (on AMG 53 models), and the plastic coolant housing assemblies. Because the M256 is a highly complex modern unit, reputable recon specialists will typically test the ISG, replace all brittle plastic coolant components with updated revisions, and perform a full software calibration as standard. For a full breakdown of market rates, see our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Mercedes-Benz M256 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: 48V Integrated Starter Generator (ISG) Failure
items.whatHappens: The ISG, which replaces the traditional alternator and starter motor, is prone to internal electrical faults or bearing wear. This triggers a "48V Electrical System Fault" warning, leading to a no-start condition, limp mode, or the engine failing to restart after an auto-stop.
items.repairVsReplace: Early ISG units were subject to manufacturer recalls and software updates. If the hardware has failed, the entire ISG unit must be replaced, which is a costly but straightforward bolt-on procedure.

items.title: Coolant Leaks (Electric Water Pump & Thermostat Housing)
items.whatHappens: The M256 utilizes several plastic coolant housing components and an electric auxiliary water pump. Over time, the constant heat cycles cause these plastic components to warp or crack, leading to external coolant leaks or internal mixing.
items.repairVsReplace: Mercedes has released updated, more durable revisions of these components. Replacing the faulty housing and pump is a standard repair, but ignoring it can lead to overheating and severe engine damage.

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch and Guide Wear
items.whatHappens: While generally robust, some early M256 engines exhibited premature timing chain stretch or guide wear, manifesting as a faint rattling noise on cold starts or camshaft position correlation fault codes.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, replacing the timing chain kit and updated guides is a known, albeit labour-intensive, repair. If ignored, it can lead to timing jumps and catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2020 M256 engines feature revised ISG hardware, updated coolant component materials, and improved timing chain tensioners, making them significantly more robust and reliable than the initial launch models .

variants.title: M256 Sub-Codes Explained - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ INTRO: The M256 family shares the same fundamental 3.0L DOHC inline-6 block architecture and 48V mild-hybrid foundation, but turbocharging strategy, auxiliary compression, and ECU mapping vary significantly between standard and AMG applications. Identifying your exact sub-code is mandatory. - Fitted to: E-Class W213 (E 450), S-Class W222/W223 (S 450, S 500), GLE-Class W167 (GLE 450) - Key technical difference: The standard-output variant, relying on a single twin-scroll turbocharger and the 48V ISG for smooth power delivery and efficiency. It lacks the electric auxiliary compressor found in AMG models. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; ISG and coolant housing leaks are the primary wear items. - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with AMG variants due to different ECU mapping, exhaust plumbing, and the absence of the electric auxiliary compressor (EAC) hardware. - Fitted to: E-Class W213 (AMG E 53), S-Class W222 (AMG S 53), AMG GT 4-Door X290 (AMG GT 53) - Key technical difference: The high-performance AMG variant. In addition to the twin-scroll turbo and ISG, it features an Electric Auxiliary Compressor (EAC) mounted at the front of the engine to eliminate turbo lag entirely, alongside a more aggressive camshaft profile and AMG-specific engine management. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; the EAC adds another potential point of electrical or mechanical failure, and the higher thermal loads can accelerate coolant component degradation. - Interchange note: Requires matching EAC hardware, specific AMG wiring harnesses, and dedicated AMG ECU calibration; not interchangeable with standard .930 variants.

variants.closing: The engine code is stamped on the right-hand side of the cylinder block, near the oil filter housing. It will also be listed on your V5C logbook under "Engine Capacity" or visible via a VIN decode. Not sure? Enter your registration above for instant confirmation.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement M256 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: Buying a used M256 engine carries significant financial risk unless it comes with a full, stamped service history and documented proof that the ISG and coolant components have been inspected or replaced under warranty. Given the high cost of modern Mercedes electronics, purchasing a used unit with unknown history is highly discouraged.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned M256 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will proactively address the common failure points by testing or replacing the ISG, upgrading all plastic coolant components to the latest revised parts, and ensuring the timing chain assembly is within strict factory tolerances.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full M156/M256 engine rebuild is highly justified for high-mileage AMG 53 models or S-Class hosts where maximum longevity, track capability, or originality is required. An upgraded rebuild should include precision balancing and the installation of the absolute latest factory-revised components.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your M256 engine is installed by specialists equipped with the latest Mercedes diagnostic software to calibrate the 48V system, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the M256 is found in modern executive and AMG vehicles valued between £25,000 and £80,000+, a full engine replacement is a financially viable necessity to protect the asset's value. However, due to the high cost of the engine and specialized labour, always ensure the replacement cost is weighed against the vehicle's current market valuation .

items.question: What is the most common failure on the M256 engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are 48V Integrated Starter Generator (ISG) failure, plastic coolant housing and electric water pump leaks, and early timing chain stretch. The ISG can trigger no-start conditions or limp mode, while degraded plastic coolant components can lead to overheating if not addressed promptly. → Get quotes for a rebuilt M256 with these issues resolved

items.question: Which Mercedes models use the M256 engine?
items.answer: The M256.930 and .940 variants were fitted to the W213 E-Class (E 450, AMG E 53), the W222/W223 S-Class (S 450, S 500, AMG S 53), the W167 GLE-Class (GLE 450, AMG GLE 53), the C257 CLS-Class (CLS 450, AMG CLS 53), and the X290 AMG GT 4-Door (AMG GT 53), serving as the definitive modern inline-6 for these chassis from 2017 onwards. → Check your registration to confirm your exact M256 fitment

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned M256 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned M256 is strongly recommended over a used unit. A proper rebuild will proactively address the common failure points by testing or replacing the 48V ISG, upgrading all plastic coolant components to the latest revised factory parts, and verifying the timing chain assembly, whereas a used engine with unknown history risks immediate, costly electrical or cooling system repairs. → Compare reconditioned M256 engine prices from UK specialists

items.question: What is the difference between M256.930 and M256.940?
items.answer: The M256.930 is the standard-output variant (found in E 450, S 450/500) relying on a single twin-scroll turbo and the 48V ISG. The M256.940 is the high-performance AMG variant (found in AMG 53 models) which adds an Electric Auxiliary Compressor (EAC) to eliminate turbo lag, alongside a more aggressive camshaft profile and AMG-specific engine management.
